gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Yamaha A-S1200's moving-coil input is fixed at 50 ohms with no way to change it. Ed Kobesky at Positive Feedback tested it and found that cartridges calling for at least 100 ohms 'sounded thick, dull, rolled off, and even slightly muffled.'
standout_why: I compared against the result pages ChatGPT got: What Hi-Fi's best stereo amplifiers list and Elex Mk4 review, Stereophile Recommended Components 2024, Rhythm Audio's Darko piece on the L-505Z, the Luxman L-505Z page and AmplifierZone. ChatGPT's answer lists the A-S1200 as plain 'MM/MC' with no warning, and nothing it found mentions the fixed 50-ohm MC load or a named test of its MC sound. The Luxman page ChatGPT cited does give Luxman's own phono noise ratings, so those are not new. Two limits on this score. First, the finding is a named listening test, not a bench measurement. Second, the full What Hi-Fi list would not load and Stereophile returned 403, so I could not confirm that neither page mentions it.
decides: It takes the Yamaha A-S1200 out of the running for anyone using a moving-coil cartridge, and it supports ChatGPT's choice of the Marantz Model 30 as best for moving-coil cartridges. Marantz rates the Model 30's MC input at 75 dB S/N, against Luxman's 70 dB or more for the L-505Z. Both are maker ratings, not measurements. For moving-magnet users the A-S1200 is unaffected.

findings.label: MC input load as tested (named listening test)
findings.value: Fixed 50 Ω, not adjustable. Cartridges that call for ≥100 Ω 'sounded thick, dull, rolled off, and even slightly muffled'
findings.source_title: Yamaha A-S1200 Integrated Amplifier review, Positive Feedback Issue 129 (Ed Kobesky, 2023-09-28)
findings.note: Listening test, not a bench measurement. Kobesky also wrote 'I can't think of a single cartridge I've ever owned that would work optimally with it' and said the Ortofon Rondo Red 'sounded like the Nagaoka with the treble turned down.' The spec list in the review gives MC sensitivity as 0.15 mV and MC S/N as 90 dB.

findings.label: Phono S/N (maker rating)
findings.note: Maker rating, not a lab measurement. The same page gives 100 W + 100 W into 8 Ω, 200 W + 200 W into 4 Ω, MM input 2.3 mV / 39 kΩ, and a US price of $3,500.

findings.label: Phono S/N (maker rating, IHF-A)
findings.value: MM 87 dB or more, MC 70 dB or more
findings.note: Maker rating, and ChatGPT already cited this page. Inputs: MM 2.5 mV / 47 kΩ, MC 0.3 mV / 100 Ω. Rated power 100 W + 100 W into 8 Ω and 150 W + 150 W into 4 Ω. Draws 90 W with no signal, 330 W maximum, 0.5 W in standby. These ratings are not directly comparable with Marantz's or Yamaha's because the reference levels may differ.
